About

A little about me.

I am from Chandler, Arizona, and I have chased the same question for as long as I can remember. What makes the brain work, and can a machine be taught to do the same? That thread runs through everything I do, from three ASU research labs to the coding bootcamps I founded at the Chandler Sunset Library.

This fall I begin Computer Science at Cal Poly San Luis Obispo, most excited by problems at the edge of AI and biology.

More about me
About

A little about me.

I am from Chandler, Arizona, and I have chased the same question for as long as I can remember. What makes the brain work, and can a machine be taught to do the same? That thread runs through everything I do.

It has led me into three ASU research labs, where I build machine learning pipelines on real colorectal cancer patient data at the Biodesign Institute, model neural dynamics with differential equations in the math department, and study protein folding for tumor biomarkers at the College of Health Solutions. Alongside the research, I teach. I founded Aztecs Who Code, grew it into city wide coding bootcamps at the Chandler Sunset Library, and as a National Ambassador for the Mark Cuban Foundation I have helped carry AI literacy across the country. This fall I begin Computer Science at Cal Poly San Luis Obispo.

Projects

Selected projects.

Nest

↗

A mobile roommate-management app: one shared home for chores, bills, groceries, and communication. Its standout feature turns a grocery run into fair, item-by-item payback. The buyer scans the receipt, Nest pulls out each item and price, everyone claims what they used, and it calculates exactly what each person owes. My team and I built Nest, and it won 1st place in the "10 Minutes Back" track at Cal Poly CodeBox Hacks.

Mobile appReceipt scanning1st Place

Predicting Colorectal Cancer Treatments

↗

A machine learning pipeline trained on 1,107 real de-identified patients from the GENIE BPC CRC dataset to predict survival, recommend chemotherapy, and flag bacterial therapy candidates. Random Forest with 5 fold cross validation reached AUC 0.68 against a 0.50 baseline. Presented at AzSEF 2026 and DataPaths.

PythonRandom ForestCancer genomics

Agent Based Modeling and Simulations

↗

Computational models of autonomous agents and emergent behavior across population growth, market dynamics, and social diffusion, built in NetLogo with MATLAB sensitivity analyses.

NetLogoMATLABABM
